title: Build Temporal-native agent-loop baseline
description: Add a minimal Python OpenAI Agents SDK plus Temporal plugin baseline to the durable vendor-session experiment. Use the same deterministic fixture, logical turn, tool destination, fault schedule, evidence, and oracle as the Claude Code and Codex arms so the study can distinguish fully Temporal-visible model/tool turns from an externally owned vendor session.
design: Extract only the relevant patterns from temporal-sa/durable-agentic-harness at pinned commit 4afef65: plugin-dispatched model calls, activity_as_tool, Workflow-minted operation IDs, destination idempotency, Signals/Queries, and child Workflow lifecycle. Do not reproduce the trading application or UI. Include client-start acknowledgement loss, model/tool Activity completion loss, destination effect loss, graceful stop versus terminate, event-stream delivery, and long-history continuation boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: The native baseline runs the same admitted logical task and faults as at least one external-vendor arm; model, tool, effect, approval, and result identities are correlated; unsafe and destination-idempotent effects are distinguished; no external-session guarantee is inferred from Workflow replay; at least three live trials per concurrency-sensitive arm and raw evidence are preserved.

title: Fold sandbox harness prior art into vendor-session plan
description: Update the durable Claude Code and Codex session plan and current Temporal surface with source-backed lessons from the May 2026 Sandbox Orchestration Harness blog, Code Exchange entry, and repository implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation identifies reusable patterns, unresolved reliability boundaries, exact new fault cases, source revision and primary links; promotional claims remain hypotheses; related experiment work is tracked in Beads; links and formatting are checked.
close_reason: Reviewed both distinct harness projects at pinned revisions, folded their reusable patterns and unresolved boundaries into the vendor-session plan and current Temporal surface, and created separate native-agent and sandbox-lifecycle experiment tasks.

title: Test Sandbox Orchestration Harness recovery boundaries
description: Use the Temporal Sandbox Orchestration Harness as prior art and a distinguishing experiment input for durable vendor coding-agent sessions. Test whether stable Workflow Update IDs, child-Workflow lifecycle state, opaque attach references, cleanup policies, and snapshot/fork behavior preserve the application invariant when provider Start or ExecuteCommand succeeds but Activity completion is lost.
design: Pin the reviewed harness commit and use a hermetic provider first. Separate outer Update deduplication from inner provider-effect idempotency. Inject exact faults after provider create/command/snapshot/stop effects and before Activity completion. Add concurrent attached-reference and parent-close-during-init cases. Treat provider capabilities and snapshot semantics as declared inputs, not interchangeable guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Unsafe controls demonstrate at least one orphan, duplicate command, or concurrent-writer violation; protected variants use stable provider operation identity or reconciliation where supported; cleanup receipt, workspace lineage, provider instance identity, snapshot identity, and current authority are independently checked; at least three admitted live trials per concurrency-sensitive arm are preserved; conclusions distinguish sandbox lifecycle durability from vendor transcript/turn and destination-effect durability.

title: Document durable vendor-agent session research plan
description: Capture the agreed Claude Code and Codex durable-session proposal in the repository, tied to experiment temporal_projects-5im and the existing guarantee/evidence methodology.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical plan document covers scope, current vendor surfaces, hypotheses, architecture, experiment arms, exact failure barriers, oracle, evidence, sequencing, product implications, and explicit non-claims; docs/research-questions.md links to it; documentation links and formatting are checked.
close_reason: Documented the canonical durable vendor-agent session experiment plan, linked it from the prioritized research agenda, and verified local references and recorded CLI interface assumptions.

title: Experiment: durable Claude Code and Codex sessions
description: Determine whether Temporal can recover a logical coding-agent session across Worker, runner, vendor process, and host failures without creating competing turns, accepting stale completion, or misreporting workspace effects. Compare a direct retryable CLI Activity, vendor resume-only recovery, and an application-fenced start-or-attach supervisor for Claude Code and Codex.
design: Invariant: at most one authorized owner may advance a logical turn or publish its result, and the accepted result must agree with independently observed workspace state. Failure boundaries include process start/vendor-ID registration, tool effect/result recording, final output/Activity completion, concurrent resume, cancellation, host loss, and version change. Oracle records logical session/turn, vendor session/thread, generation/capability, Temporal attempt, runner/process, ordered vendor events, workspace hashes/diffs, physical effects, and UTC times. The unsafe direct-subprocess arm must violate at least one invariant. Vendor resume-only and fenced start-or-attach remain separate arms. A session-resume feature is not treated as exactly-once effects.
acceptance_criteria: A written experiment contract distinguishes transcript, turn/process, and workspace/effect durability; documents current Claude Code and Codex interfaces with dated primary sources; specifies exact barriers, three experimental arms, negative control, falsifiers, evidence fields, trial admission, and product decision criteria; implementation preserves at least three independent live trials per concurrency-sensitive arm and updates the guarantee ledger only from observed evidence.
notes: Canonical plan: docs/plans/durable-vendor-agent-sessions.md. Vendor interfaces were locally verified against Codex CLI 0.147.0 and Claude Code 2.1.224 on 2026-08-07. Prior-art review is pinned to temporal-sa/durable-agentic-harness@4afef65 and temporal-community/sandbox-orchestration-harness@e8a8854. The former adds a Temporal-native OpenAI Agents baseline (temporal_projects-5im.4); the latter adds sandbox lifecycle calibration (temporal_projects-5im.2). Neither is durability evidence for external vendor sessions. Do not upgrade the prospective claim until negative controls and protected arms produce admitted live trials.

title: Audit and publish public Agent Durability Lab repository
description: Review the local repository and pending changes for public-release suitability, remove or exclude secrets/internal-only material, run quality and evidence gates, commit the intended public content, and push it to the user-authorized GitHub repository.
design: Treat the GitHub remote as a public disclosure boundary. Inventory committed and uncommitted files, inspect evidence and Beads data for sensitive content, scan history and working tree for secrets, verify licenses/source provenance, preserve append-only experiment evidence, and push only after checks pass.
acceptance_criteria: Remote target is verified; no secrets or unintended private/internal content are published; intended docs, benchmark contract, implementation, tests, and qualifying evidence are committed; repository gates pass; pushed branch and commit are reported; any excluded material is documented.
notes: Public release completed and verified at https://github.com/sjarmak/temporal_projects. Remote main matches the audited local branch; the MIT license and public module path are correct; runtime DBs, binaries, coverage files, and raw capabilities remain excluded; history and staged secret scans were clean; build, vet, race, live-experiment, replay, and all 80% coverage gates passed.
close_reason: Public release audited and prepared: remote/license verified, public module path aligned, private runtime artifacts excluded, source/docs/benchmark/evidence reviewed, secret scans clean, and build/vet/race/coverage gates passed.

title: Write shareable Gas City and Agent Durability Lab findings brief
description: Create a concise repository document for Temporal engineering, developer advocacy, and product audiences. Trace claims from Gas City operational evidence and the lab's six reproduced findings, distinguish prior observation from controlled evidence, list limits, and map the remaining Beads-backed research plan.
design: Use Gas City as the motivating field system and Agent Durability Lab as controlled reproduction. Organize around responsibility boundaries, direct findings, product implications, safe public wording, limitations, and ordered remaining work. Keep the note self-contained and shareable without internal paths or personal details.
acceptance_criteria: Document cites local source evidence, separates observed findings from hypotheses, gives audience-specific implications, includes remaining planned work and comparison program, avoids unsupported Temporal guarantees, and passes documentation/repository checks.
notes: Expanded further with Engineering Reliable Coding Agents draft principles. The brief now separates book synthesis from field/lab evidence and applies authority-boundary, unknown-state, measured recovery, independent verification, typed-event, rebuildable-memory, gate-causal-power, and failure-attribution principles. Added follow-up beads temporal_projects-k4x and temporal_projects-uju; extended l7e observability notes.
close_reason: Published the shareable repository brief with Gas City field evidence, six lab findings, Temporal audience implications, benchmark methodology from CodeScaleBench/EnterpriseBench/codeprobe, book-derived reliability principles, source provenance, limits, and the Beads-backed remaining plan. Updated the benchmark contract admission and validity gates; all local links, cited source paths, JSON, and diff checks pass.

title: Implement common cross-system durability harness
description: Implement contract-v1 common simulator protocol, authority store, effect destination, named fault controller, evidence envelope, and independent oracle without importing any system adapter.
design: Follow benchmarks/agent-durability/contract-v1.json. This is common infrastructure, not a new generic agent framework.
acceptance_criteria: All four benchmark cases run against a calibration adapter; protocol and evidence schemas are validated; the oracle cannot be written by adapters; invalid and failed runs are preserved; three deterministic development trials pass.
notes: Schema/oracle calibration foundation implemented. contract-v1 now names exact raw evidence files; protocol, deterministic calibration emitter, CLI suite runner, and independent oracle exist with three trials for all four cases across unfaulted/unsafe/protected probes. Current evidence is calibration-20260807-v4: 24 valid-pass and 12 expected valid-fail. v1-v3 are preserved and documented as superseded after adversarial reviews found fail-open validation; every finding is now a regression test. Full go test -race ./... and make coverage pass; core harness coverage is 83.4%. Remaining before closing: extract the append-only raw writer into a public common adapter API and connect the existing live simulator, authority store, effect destination, named barrier, and process controller to the v1 evidence contract.

title: Run and publish first cross-system agent durability comparison
description: After all four adapters conform, execute the publication matrix and write a comparison that answers correctness and responsibility boundaries before efficiency.
design: Report native-minimum, portable-safety, and native-optimized tracks separately. Add systems only if their architecture changes a decision exposed by wave one.
acceptance_criteria: At least 30 fresh randomized-order trials per required arm; raw/invalid/failed runs retained; output parity gates latency/cost comparisons; uncertainty and version pins reported; no scalar winner; conclusions link directly to evidence and falsifiers.

title: Test Worker death after exec before process registration
description: The launch-gap experiment closes the pre-exec phantom. It does not establish discovery or cleanup when the OS child starts and Worker death occurs before the child registers. Construct this later boundary with a child-side pre-registration barrier, then test fenced replacement, stale registration rejection, surviving-process discovery, and cleanup/credential revocation.
acceptance_criteria: A real child survives Worker SIGKILL while blocked before registration; retry behavior is reproduced under control and fenced recovery; stale registration/effects fail closed; process discovery and cleanup observations are preserved; destination/credential assumptions are explicit.
notes: Final v3 matrix: three attach-control and three fenced-replacement trials on Temporal Server 1.31.2 / Go SDK 1.47.0. All six captured pre-kill store state as generation-1 launch_pending with PID 0 while an exact live child PID/start identity existed. Attach reused the child; replacement completed generation 2, rejected the old exact registration, and observed cooperative exit. V1 is excluded for the stale protocol label; v2 is excluded for lacking standalone pre-kill snapshots. Full race suite, coverage gates, vet, staticcheck, module verification, and govulncheck pass.
close_reason: Six final live trials satisfy the post-exec boundary oracle; exact process discovery, attach/replacement behavior, stale registration rejection, cleanup observation, replay, evidence, and responsibility/credential limits are documented.

title: Experiment: external effect succeeds before Activity completion is lost
description: Build the next failure-boundary experiment: an external effect succeeds, the Worker dies before Temporal records Activity completion, and retry observes ambiguity. Compare an idempotent endpoint, a non-idempotent endpoint, a transactional database mutation, Git/worktree mutation, message publication, and artifact creation without claiming exactly-once behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Each destination has a stated invariant, exact post-effect/pre-completion barrier, unsafe control, destination-specific protected mechanism, repeated race-enabled live trials, raw evidence, responsibility split, and falsifier; docs/guarantees.md and findings are updated.
notes: Completed live crash-window matrix on Temporal Server 1.31.2/API 1.63.4/SDK 1.47.0. Preserved 36 valid race-enabled trials: three unsafe and three protected for each of six destinations. Every unsafe run produced two physical effects despite one Temporal completion; every protected run produced one effect and reused the receipt through destination-specific idempotency, transaction, or reconciliation. Preserved two invalid harness runs as excluded evidence. Validation: make coverage (core 85.1%, completion lab 81.9%, external-effects lab 80.9%), go vet, staticcheck, module verification, govulncheck, 36 JSON verdict audits, six Git bundle verifications, replay test, diff check, and focused security/correctness review with no remaining critical or high findings. Real broker semantics, concurrent same-ID reconciliation, and narrower artifact/Git windows remain explicitly unresolved.
close_reason: Reproduced the post-effect/pre-completion crash window across six destination classes, preserved unsafe and protected evidence, added fail-closed tests and replay coverage, and documented the responsibility boundary without claiming exactly once.

title: Reconcile launch decisions without registered child processes
description: The application store records a launch decision before the OS child is successfully started and registered. If launch fails or the Worker dies in that window, reattachment can wait forever on a phantom executor. Add a deterministic experiment before changing the protocol.
acceptance_criteria: A failing reproduction kills/fails between durable launch decision and process registration; the evidence preserves the phantom-owner failure; the minimal recovery protocol distinguishes pending launch from live registered executor and either safely retries launch or replaces with fencing.
notes:
Independent milestone review confirmed the current reattach protocol can wait on a durable launch decision whose child never registered. This remains deliberately unfixed until its failure is captured at an exact post-decision/pre-launch or pre-registration barrier; do not add a PID-missing heuristic.
Completed exact post-launch-decision/pre-process-launch reproduction. Preserved v1/v2 development evidence and final v3 control/recovery evidence. The control records an attempt-2 attachment to a PID-less launch_pending executor; indefinite waiting is an implementation inference, while server-visible retry heartbeat remains unresolved in temporal_projects-79z. The minimal protocol adds explicit launch_pending/running/completed lifecycle, fenced conditional replacement only for pending launches, monotonic Temporal-attempt checks, registration-gated mutation, and exact barrier identity validation. Final v3 recovery has one accepted generation-2 effect/outcome and matching Workflow/application results. Validation: go test -race -timeout 4m ./..., 85.1% coverage, go vet, staticcheck, go mod verify, govulncheck, replay tests, evidence JSON validation, and independent code/security reviews with no CRITICAL or HIGH findings.

title: Experiment: CompleteActivityByID stale-attempt semantics
description: Construct a live reproduction for source-observed CompleteActivityByID behavior after an Activity retry. Separate stale original task-token completion, completion by logical Activity ID, and application-level stale-writer fencing.
acceptance_criteria: A real Temporal service test captures the old attempt, forces retry, attempts both completion paths, records exact service responses/history, and documents observed semantics without extrapolating beyond the tested Server/SDK versions.
notes: Completed live reproduction on Temporal Server 1.31.2/API 1.63.4/SDK 1.47.0. Final v2 evidence has three independent trials per arm. Stale attempt-1 task tokens returned *serviceerror.NotFound; CompleteActivityByID accepted the attempt-1 result and completed the current pending logical Activity; the durable opaque-capability fence rejected attempt 1 before an RPC. V1 is preserved as pre-review evidence after review found submitted_at was captured after RPC return; v2 records request/response timestamps and all accepted completion event times fall inside them. Validation: full go test -race ./..., replay, 85.1% core and 81.9% experiment coverage, vet, staticcheck, module verification, govulncheck, evidence/token/permission checks, and independent correctness/security/simplification reviews with no remaining CRITICAL/HIGH findings.
close_reason: Observed task-token versus logical-ID completion semantics, added application fencing control, preserved repeated evidence, and documented the guarantee boundary.

title: Milestone 1: worker death with surviving agent
description:
## Why
Establish the Agent Durability Lab and produce executable evidence for a Temporal Activity whose Worker dies while an independently running agent process survives.

## Scope
Create operating guidance and minimum research documentation; implement deterministic unsafe, stable-identity/reattachment, and fenced-ownership variants; preserve event evidence; integrate with the Temporal Go SDK; and test the precise failure boundaries without sleep-based coordination.
design: Single-machine laboratory. Use a durable application work store for logical sessions/generations and an append-only JSONL event ledger. Use explicit named barriers for failure injection. Keep Temporal workflow orchestration thin and deterministic. Run Temporal SDK testsuite for Workflow/Activity contract plus a subprocess E2E harness for launcher death; document where a live Temporal service remains required for true Worker-process death validation.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md contain concise lab rules; guarantees and methodology docs distinguish Temporal, application, and external-system responsibility; tests first demonstrate duplicate writers in unsafe mode, reattachment by stable session identity, and stale-completion rejection by fencing; a real child process can outlive its launcher; a Temporal workflow/activity integration test proves retry after lost Activity completion; deterministic repeated trials pass under go test -race ./... with at least 80% package coverage; control evidence and findings are preserved.
notes: Completed with final v3 evidence under Go 1.25.12. Final verification: go test -race -timeout 4m ./... (two live trials per arm), make coverage 84.7%, go vet, staticcheck, go mod verify, and govulncheck clean. Independent code/simplification/security reviews completed; HIGH findings were fixed and re-verified. Original and v2 evidence remain preserved; docs point to v3.
close_reason: Milestone acceptance satisfied: real Worker death/surviving child experiment, unsafe/reattach/fenced evidence, replay/nondeterminism checks, repeated race trials, 84.7% core coverage, findings/guarantees, and reviewed security remediations are complete.

title: Experiment: destination-enforced revocation after executor replacement
description: Test the book's authority-boundary claim against stale agent execution. Replace an owner while the old process remains alive or partitioned, then attempt mutations with copied destination credentials. Determine which API, Git, database, or capability mechanisms actually revoke authority at the destination rather than only in the application work store.
design: Use an unsafe copied-credential control, a destination-enforced scoped capability arm, and explicit ordinary/recovery identity separation. Inject replacement and delayed stale mutation at named barriers. Record the full reachable-authority graph and test permitted plus prohibited directions.
acceptance_criteria: At least one real local destination rejects an obsolete executor at its enforcement boundary; unsafe control demonstrates continued stale authority; cancellation/replacement and recovery identities are distinct; repeated evidence and falsifier are documented; no generic credential-revocation claim is made.

title: Experiment: recurring faults and cumulative recovery degradation
description: Extend recovery testing beyond independent one-kill trials. Inject a sequence of named faults during one continuing long-running agent operation and compare it with clean-start faulted runs to expose leaked leases, retry backlog, enlarged history, cache churn, and recovery changes by fault ordinal.
design: Freeze workload and configuration, predeclare fault sequence, use exact barriers, retain fault ordinal, and measure detection-to-next-correct-state latency, accepted effects, stale actions, queue/history growth, and operator intervention. Keep independent clean-start trials as the control for accumulated state.
acceptance_criteria: Multiple faults occur in one valid continuing run at exact barriers; an independent-run control exists; correctness and recovery metrics are reported by fault ordinal; missed boundaries are invalid rather than passes; raw evidence and falsifier are preserved.

title: Implement contract-conformant Temporal benchmark adapter
description: Map the cross-system benchmark contract to current Temporal Workflow/Activity and declared Standalone Activity variants, reusing existing evidence where protocols match but rerunning every conformant case.
design: Keep durable procedure in Temporal and application safety mechanisms explicitly tagged. Compare Workflow orchestration with Standalone Activity only where both can represent the case.
acceptance_criteria: Native-minimum and portable-safety tracks pass conformance; all four faults preserve Temporal Event History plus common evidence; versions and non-default options are pinned; no guarantee is inferred from prior non-conformant runs.

title: Implement Restate agent durability benchmark adapter
description: Implement Restate Go native-minimum and portable-safety adapters for all four contract-v1 cases using current services/workflows, durable Run, journal, and invocation APIs as appropriate.
design: Use Restate idiomatically but do not replace the common agent, destination, fault controller, or oracle. Treat documented behavior as a hypothesis until reproduced.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter passes the conformance gate and three development trials per case/track; exports Restate journal/invocation evidence; records exact versions/timeouts/retry settings; observed results distinguish journal guarantees from external effect and process guarantees.

title: Implement DBOS Go agent durability benchmark adapter
description: Implement DBOS Go native-minimum and portable-safety adapters for all four contract-v1 cases, plus a separately labeled native-optimized datasource transaction arm where applicable.
design: Do not compare a datasource-transaction optimized arm against another system's minimum arm. The common external destination remains fixed in required tracks.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter passes the conformance gate and three development trials per case/required track; exports DBOS workflow/step evidence; separates at-least-once steps from atomic datasource transactions; pins Postgres and DBOS versions and recovery configuration.

title: Implement PostgreSQL queue lease outbox benchmark adapter
description: Implement the minimal PostgreSQL durability baseline for contract-v1 using explicit queue rows, leases/generations, transactions, and outbox/reconciliation where declared.
design: This is a transparent DIY baseline, not a framework. Keep orchestration minimal and expose operator/recovery work rather than hiding it in helper abstractions.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter passes the conformance gate and three development trials per case/track; schema and SQL migrations are tested; lease expiry/recovery and SKIP LOCKED behavior are evidenced; every guarantee is attributed to concrete SQL/application logic.

title: Define cross-system agent durability benchmark contract
description: Design a portable black-box benchmark that compares reliable long-running agent execution across Temporal, Restate, DBOS Go, and a minimal PostgreSQL queue/lease/outbox implementation. The benchmark must compare application correctness after recovery rather than feature lists or marketing claims.
design: Use the same external contract, not the same internal architecture. Reuse the strongest surviving-executor, ambiguous-effect, fencing, and cancellation boundaries. Temporal is the baseline; Restate, DBOS Go, and PostgreSQL queue/lease/outbox are wave one. Defer Durable Task and cloud-only systems until a later wave. This issue designs the contract and queue only; it does not implement comparator adapters.
acceptance_criteria: The contract fixes common agent workload, external destinations, invariant, fault boundary, evidence schema, oracle, and operational measurements while allowing idiomatic system-specific adapters; initial comparator assumptions are grounded in current primary documentation; a follow-up Bead exists for each adapter and for the final comparison; no unimplemented system is credited with a guarantee.
notes: Completed benchmarks/agent-durability contract v1. It fixes the simulator, authority/destination/failure/oracle protocols; defines native-minimum, portable-safety, and optional native-optimized tracks; specifies four exact cases, evidence, invalid-run rules, parity-gated metrics, and 3-development/30-publication trial policy; and links current primary sources without crediting unimplemented guarantees. Follow-up Beads: y33.1 common harness, y33.2 Temporal, y33.3 Restate, y33.4 DBOS Go, y33.5 PostgreSQL, y33.6 final comparison. All adapters depend on the harness and the comparison depends on all adapters; dependency graph is acyclic.
close_reason: Acceptance satisfied: mechanism-neutral cross-system contract, current primary-source hypotheses, independent oracle/evidence schema, fair trial and measurement policy, and complete dependent adapter/comparison Bead queue.

title: Observe heartbeat visibility during phantom reattachment
description: A stronger launch-gap control attempted to wait until DescribeWorkflowExecution exposed heartbeat details for Activity attempt 2 before cancellation. One of two live trials reached the overall deadline without that exact observation. Build a focused reproduction that distinguishes SDK heartbeat calls, server-persisted heartbeat details, Activity attempt compaction, and Describe visibility without upgrading inference to observation.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve the failing/variable history and Describe snapshots; use an exact synchronization protocol; state which heartbeat call and attempt the server durably observed; document what can and cannot be used as an operator liveness signal.

title: Harden failure-injection evidence authenticity
description: The loopback barrier trusts all same-host processes. A local process can forge the first arrival and cause the controller to inject a fault at a false boundary. Add identity binding only when experiments move beyond a trusted single-user lab.
acceptance_criteria: The controller pre-registers expected session/generation/actor/barrier identities, requests are authenticated with per-run credentials, forged/replayed arrivals fail closed, and raw credentials never enter portable evidence.

title: Experiment: agent session compatibility across Worker Versioning deployments
description: Run long-lived external sessions across pinned and auto-upgrade Worker deployments; distinguish Workflow replay compatibility, Activity implementation compatibility, and the detached agent protocol/build contract.
acceptance_criteria: Replay-safe and deliberately incompatible changes are tested on a real service; retry/reattachment across versions records Worker deployment and agent-build identity; incompatible attachment fails closed.

title: Experiment: partial Workflow Stream output and retry reconstruction
description: Measure consumer-observed prefixes, publisher identity, duplicate output, buffered-event loss, ordering, and resumption when a Worker dies during Workflow Stream publication.
acceptance_criteria: Current Public Preview API is used; exact stream boundaries and durable consumer observations are preserved; retries test publisher identity and duplicate handling; conclusions state what lives in history versus external state.

title: Experiment: large artifact write/reference/acknowledgement windows
description: Test large output and code-patch artifacts across object write, reference creation, reference persistence, Activity completion, and consumer acknowledgement failures, including Temporal External Storage where applicable.
acceptance_criteria: Each boundary has an orphan/loss/duplication oracle, content hashes and durable references are recorded, cleanup/reconciliation is explicit, and payload size is kept out of Workflow history where intended.

title: Compare Workflow orchestration with Standalone Activity durability
description: Implement matched experiments using a Workflow plus Activity and a current Standalone Activity to answer when durable execution is sufficient versus when a durable orchestration state machine adds necessary state/order.
acceptance_criteria: The same effect/failure invariant runs through both primitives on supported current versions; operational state, replay value, retry semantics, and failure behavior are measured and documented.

title: Experiment: precise cancellation across Worker death and ownership change
description: Test cancellation for healthy Worker, killed Worker with surviving child, temporarily unreachable child, owner replacement, and cancellation/completion races. Cancellation must name session and generation and fail closed for stale executors.
design: Cancellation has two distinct operations. Logical-session cancellation is a durable terminal transition that revokes the current generation, rejects later progress/effects/outcomes, prevents replacement, and races with completion by first committed store transition. Executor stop targets an exact session/generation/PID/start identity and must not affect a replacement. Record request, durable revocation, delivery attempt, acknowledgement, and confirmed process-tree disposition separately. Compare Temporal WaitForCancellation false/true. Exercise healthy Worker, Worker death with surviving child, temporarily unreachable/frozen child, ownership change and stale delayed stop, both cancellation/completion orderings, and an agent-spawned long-lived descendant. Prefer cooperative shutdown, pidfd exact-leader escalation, and isolated process-group descendant cleanup; defer cgroups unless process groups cannot support a sound single-host conclusion. Use exact barriers and at least three live trials for timing-sensitive arms.
acceptance_criteria: Each cancellation boundary uses deterministic coordination, proves the exact targeted process/generation, records delivery and acknowledgement separately, and documents what Temporal versus the application guarantees.
notes: Completed with final v2 evidence at experiments/cancellation/evidence/cancellation-20260807-v2-*: 24 valid live trials, comprising 6 Temporal-only controls and 18 application-revoked safe runs across both WaitForCancellation policies. Added first-terminal-wins cancellation, exact session/generation/owner/PID/start/group targeting, separate delivery and acknowledgement, leader/tool-child process-tree tests, Worker-death and frozen-agent arms, history/evidence oracles, replay coverage, and finding 0006. Security review replaced raw lab freeze/cleanup group signals with the exact-identity controller and added safe run-ID validation. Verified by go test -race ./..., make coverage (83.8% core), go vet, staticcheck, go mod verify, govulncheck, diff hygiene, and evidence capability scan.
close_reason: Acceptance satisfied: deterministic exact-boundary cancellation matrix, 24 final live trials, application revocation and terminal-race tests, exact process-tree and stale-stop controls, Temporal history evidence, documented responsibility split, and clean quality/security gates.

title: Experiment: observability of wedged agents versus legitimate waits
description: Define and test application signals that distinguish healthy Temporal retry, permanently failing retry, live-but-wedged child, dead Worker with healthy child, stale executor, ambiguous effect, and legitimate Workflow wait.
acceptance_criteria: A single-machine operator can classify each injected state from preserved Temporal and application signals without inspecting process internals; false-positive/false-negative observations and blind spots are documented.
notes: Book-derived extension: make the operator model consume versioned typed events with causal identities; keep raw evidence distinct from derived views; expose missing events as trace failures; evolve the schema from questions failed investigations cannot answer.
